What it's for. A built-in notification feed keeps the student informed of the events in their journey (offers, validations, messages), with read-on-open, a "mark all as read" action and a live unread counter.

Who it's for. student

How it works. The page lists the most recent notifications; opening one marks it as read; "mark all as read" processes the whole set and returns to the previous page. A counter feeds the badge.

Use case.

A student receives a notification that their OLA has been validated and clicks through to see the details.

docs.title: EWP network (Erasmus Without Paper)
docs.text:
EWP (Erasmus Without Paper) is the European interoperability standard that lets international relations offices exchange their mobility data fully digitally, with no paper and no manual emails. AroundLink connects your institution to this network: your inter-institutional agreements, learning agreements, transcripts of records and nominations flow directly software-to-software with your partner universities. Concretely, an agreement signed on your side appears at the partner's, a grade entered here travels to the student's home university, and every change notifies the other side automatically.

Are you on the IT / integration team?

This page describes the value of each building block. For the list of endpoints, methods, API versions and links to the official EWP specifications, see the EWP API reference.

docs.title: Discovery / Manifest
docs.text:
What it's for. The manifest is your institution's digital business card on the EWP network. It tells every partner university which services you offer and how to reach you reliably. Without it, no partner can discover you or exchange anything with you.

Who it's for. partner institution / admin

How it works. AroundLink publishes and maintains this manifest for your institution. A partner (or the network's central directory) reads it to learn that you can exchange agreements, learning agreements, transcripts and nominations, then establishes a trust relationship. Everything is automatic — you have nothing to publish by hand.

Use case.

A Spanish university adds you as a partner; its software reads your manifest and immediately discovers it can send you a digital agreement.

docs.title: Echo
docs.text:
What it's for. Echo is a connectivity test: it confirms that your institution and a partner can reach and mutually authenticate each other. It's the diagnostic tool used when connecting a new partner, before any real data flows.

Who it's for. partner institution / admin

How it works. A test call returns exactly the information sent, together with the verified identity of the caller. A correct response proves that the link and the trust between the two institutions are working.

Use case.

During partner onboarding, the team sends an Echo call; a successful response confirms the trust handshake is operational.

docs.title: Institutions
docs.text:
What it's for. This building block publishes your institution's basic identity (its official name) from its identifier. It lets partners display a readable name instead of a technical code in their screens.

Who it's for. partner institution

How it works. A partner supplies one or more institution identifiers and gets back the matching names. Its interfaces can then present your agreements and mobilities with a human-readable label.

Use case.

A partner shows "Institut Polytechnique des Sciences Avancées" next to an incoming agreement, rather than the institution's technical identifier.

docs.title: Factsheet (institution info sheet)
docs.text: The factsheet is your institution's practical info sheet: nomination and application deadlines, housing / visa / insurance contacts, accessibility, decision and transcript turnaround limits. AroundLink covers three complementary uses.

docs.title: Publish your factsheet
docs.text:
What it's for. You broadcast your practical information to the whole network, so partners can advise their outgoing students without having to email you.

Who it's for. partner institution

How it works. As soon as a partner requests your sheet, AroundLink generates it from the information entered by your office and returns it in a network-compliant format.

Use case.

A partner reads your factsheet and sees your application deadlines without having to email the international relations office.

docs.title: Edit your factsheet
docs.text:
What it's for. From a simple form, you maintain the content of the sheet that will be broadcast to all your partners.

Who it's for. IRO manager

How it works. From the dedicated screen in your workspace, you fill in and update the sheet's sections. Incorrectly filled fields (for example a phone number without a country prefix) are flagged before saving.

Use case.

The IRO manager updates the spring-semester nomination dates; the new sheet is immediately available to partners.

docs.title: Fetch a partner's factsheet
docs.text:
What it's for. You import a partner's practical sheet on demand, to find its dates and contacts directly in AroundLink instead of looking them up elsewhere.

Who it's for. IRO manager

How it works. From a partner institution's page, a sync action fetches its factsheet from the network and stores it on your side. Fields you have locked manually are never overwritten; if the partner exposes no sheet, your hand-entered data is kept.

Use case.

Before a campaign, the manager syncs a partner's factsheet to display its decision turnaround directly in the agreement file.

docs.title: IIA — inter-institutional agreements
docs.text:
Exchanging inter-institutional agreements (IIA) is the flagship function: negotiate, compare and sign bilateral Erasmus+ agreements without paper, with a shared copy between both institutions. This maps to agreements in AroundLink.

What it's for. You manage an agreement's entire lifecycle — content, mobility conditions, contacts, signing dates — digitally and shared with the partner. No more divergent PDF versions traded by email: both sides work from a single reference.

Who it's for. IRO manager / partner institution

How it works. The partner can list and view the agreements it shares with you. Each institution approves the exact version it has in front of it; when both have approved, the agreement is in effect. Any change on one side automatically notifies the other, which fetches the fresh version.

Use case.

You adjust the number of places on an agreement; the partner is notified, fetches the new version, approves it, and the agreement flips to "in effect" on both sides.

docs.title: Change notification (CNR) and review
docs.text:
What it's for. When a partner modifies an agreement, you are notified and you decide field by field what you accept, rather than suffering an automatic overwrite. It's the safeguard that protects the integrity of your data.

Who it's for. IRO manager

How it works. A change notification triggers fetching the partner's version. AroundLink prepares a side-by-side comparison and stages the proposal for review (never applied automatically); the coordinator is notified by email. They accept the desired fields — the agreement then returns to draft for a fresh approval — or reject without touching their data.

Use case.

A partner changes a language of instruction; the coordinator sees the difference, accepts that single change and leaves the rest unchanged.

docs.title: OLA — learning agreements
docs.text:
Digital exchange and co-signing of the learning agreements (OLA) for the students you send on mobility. See also the Learning Agreement page.

What it's for. You publish your outgoing students' learning agreements — courses studied, courses recognised on return, signatures — so the host university reviews and signs them online. The validation round-trip happens without paper.

Who it's for. IRO manager / coordinator / partner institution

How it works. The host university can list and fetch your students' agreements, then approve them or request changes. On approval, its signature is recorded; when both sides have signed, the agreement is validated. If the partner reports a change on its side, AroundLink automatically fetches the up-to-date version.

Use case.

The host university approves a student's learning agreement online; the status turns to "validated" in AroundLink and recognition is set in motion.

docs.title: Transcript (ToR — transcript of records)
docs.text:
Digital sending of transcripts for the students you host, back to their home university. See also Transcript of Records.

What it's for. You transmit the official transcript (courses, grades, ECTS credits, pass / fail) of your incoming students, so their home institution imports the results and grants recognition without a paper transcript.

Who it's for. coordinator / partner institution

How it works. The home institution can list and fetch the transcripts of its students who studied with you. The transcript is transmitted in a standardised European format, ready to be imported and recognised automatically.

Use case.

After exams, the partner's software fetches its student's transcript and automatically recognises the credits earned.

docs.title: Nominations (outgoing mobilities)
docs.text:
Digital nomination of the students you send to a partner, and receipt of its decision. See also affectation.

What it's for. You transmit each outgoing student nomination (identity, field of study, level, linked agreement) so the host university accepts or rejects it digitally, with a tracked history of the decision.

Who it's for. IRO manager / partner institution

How it works. The host university can list and view the nominations you send it, then approve or reject them. The decision comes back into AroundLink and updates the student's status, with a record of the signer or the rejection reason.

Use case.

You nominate a student to Milan; the Milan office approves via the network and the student's status turns to "approved" in AroundLink, with the signer recorded.

docs.title: Technical foundations
docs.text:
What it's for. Beneath every exchange sit the mechanisms that guarantee data reaches the right partner, intact and from a certified source. They are invisible to the user but essential to the network's trust.

Who it's for. admin

How it works. Every message exchanged is signed and verified, so each institution knows with certainty who is talking to it. A central network directory makes it possible to find each partner's address and identity before transmitting anything.

Use case.

Before sending an agreement, AroundLink queries the directory to locate the partner and signs the message so it is accepted as authentic.

docs.title: EWP API reference (IT / integrators)
docs.text:
Who this page is for

This page is technical: it is aimed at IT departments, integration teams and partners connecting their system to AroundLink over the EWP network. For the business value of each building block, see the Overview page.

AroundLink implements the EWP (Erasmus Without Paper) network APIs to exchange agreements, learning agreements, transcripts and nominations with partner universities, without manual intervention.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
• All incoming APIs (a partner calls us) are exposed under ‌/ewp/{hei-id}/…, where {hei-id} is the HEI identifier of the relevant AroundLink client institution.
  • Two directions:
    • Incoming — the partner's system (or the EWP Registry) calls AroundLink.
    • Outgoing — AroundLink calls the partner (fetch / notify).
  • Authentication — exchanges are signed (HTTP Signature, the standard EWP mechanism on both client and server). The caller is identified by its public key declared in the EWP Registry; that identity is what scopes the data (a partner only sees the objects that concern it).
  • Discovery — a partner finds the institution and its services via the manifest; it can check connectivity and authentication via Echo before any real exchange.
  • CNR (Change Notification Receiver) — lightweight "this object changed, come and re-fetch it" notifications; they keep both copies in sync.

docs.title: How to test the connection
docs.text: A signed call to ‌/ewp/{hei-id}/echo returns the parameters passed and the authenticated HEI identity of the caller. A 200 with the correct HEI confirms that the link and signature work — the first step of any onboarding.

docs.title: Incoming endpoints (partner → AroundLink)
docs.text: Paths relative to ‌/ewp/{hei-id}.

docs.title: Discovery & diagnostics
docs.text: Endpoint Method API (version) Role /manifest.xml GET Discovery v6 Manifest: lists the implemented APIs, their URLs and versions, the contact and the signing public keys. Entry point of any onboarding. /echo GET · POST Echo v2 Connectivity + authentication test; echoes back the authenticated caller. /institutions GET · POST Institutions v2 Resolves one or more HEI identifiers to institution names (up to 10). /factsheet GET · POST Factsheet v1.2 Serves the institution's fact sheet (deadlines, housing/visa contacts, turnaround limits).

docs.title: IIA — inter-institutional agreements
docs.text: Endpoint Method API (version) Role /iias/index GET · POST IIAs v7 Lists the identifiers of agreements shared with the caller (filters: partner, year, modified since). /iias/get GET · POST IIAs v7 Full content of one or more agreements (up to 100), with the version hash. /iias/approval GET · POST iias-approval v2 Our approval (id + hash of the approved version) for the caller's agreements. /iias/stats GET IIAs v7 Approval statistics (fetchable, approved by one / both sides…). /iia-cnr POST iia-cnr v3 Notification: an agreement changed on the partner side → we re-fetch it for review. /iia-approval-cnr POST iia-approval-cnr v2 Notification: the partner approved → we re-fetch its approval.

docs.title: OLA — learning agreements (outgoing mobilities)
docs.text: Endpoint Method API (version) Role /omobility-las/index GET · POST omobility-las v1.2 Lists our outgoing students' learning agreements for the calling receiving institution. /omobility-las/get GET · POST omobility-las v1.2 Full content of a learning agreement (courses, signatures, change proposals). Restricted to the receiving institution. /omobility-las/update POST omobility-las v1.2 The receiving institution approves or requests changes (signature / comment). /omobility-las/stats GET omobility-las v1.2 Per-year counters (approved / rejected / pending). /omobility-la-cnr POST omobility-la-cnr v1 Notification: a learning agreement changed on the partner side → re-fetch.

docs.title: ToR — transcripts of records (incoming mobilities)
docs.text: Endpoint Method API (version) Role /imobility-tors/index GET · POST imobility-tors v1 Lists the transcripts of incoming students for the calling home institution. /imobility-tors/get GET · POST imobility-tors v1 Official transcript in ELMO format (courses, grades, ECTS). Restricted to the home institution. /imobility-tors/stats GET imobility-tor-stats v1 Transcript counters per year. /imobility-tor-cnr POST imobility-tor-cnr v1 Notification: a transcript changed → re-fetch.

docs.title: Nominations (outgoing mobilities)
docs.text: Endpoint Method API (version) Role /omobilities/index GET · POST omobilities v3 Lists the student nominations we send to the calling receiving institution. /omobilities/get GET · POST omobilities v3 Nomination detail (student identity, ISCED-F field, EQF level, linked agreement, status). Restricted to the receiving institution. /omobilities/update POST omobilities v3 The receiving institution accepts or rejects the nomination; the decision flows back into AroundLink. /omobility-cnr POST omobility-cnr v1 Notification: a nomination changed → re-fetch.

docs.title: Outgoing calls (AroundLink → partner)
docs.text:
Triggered automatically by AroundLink (when an object is edited, or when a CNR is received). They use the partner's service URL, resolved via the EWP Registry, and are signed with our credentials.

Action Trigger Effect Fetch an agreement (IIA) CNR received / sync Fetches the partner's version and prepares a review. Fetch an IIA approval Approval CNR received Updates the partner's approval state. Notify an IIA change An agreement edited on our side Sends an iia-cnr to the partner. Fetch / notify an OLA Edit / CNR Synchronises the learning agreement. Fetch a transcript (ToR) CNR received Updates the transcript. Fetch a nomination CNR received Updates the nomination and its decision. Fetch a partner factsheet Manual action by the IRO Imports the partner's deadlines/contacts into AroundLink.

docs.title: Foundations
docs.text:
• HTTP signature (client + server) — every request and response is signed and verified (short time window). The key fingerprint identifies the caller and drives data scoping.
  • EWP Registry (local mirror) — catalogue of the network's institutions, APIs, versions and public keys; used to resolve a partner's URL before an outgoing call and to identify the caller of an incoming call.
  • ECHE list (mirror) — the Erasmus Charter, used as an institution source.

Onboarding good practice

  1. Add the institution (its HEI ID) on the partner side. 2. Read the manifest.xml to discover services and keys. 3. Validate the link with a signed echo. 4. Move on to the real exchanges (IIA, OLA, ToR, nominations).

docs.title: AroundLink REST API
docs.text:
Beyond EWP, AroundLink exposes its own REST API (API Platform / Hydra) for its business resources (agreements, students, learning agreements, transcripts…). Its interactive documentation — contract, resources and schemas, always up to date — is generated automatically:

  • AroundLink API documentation (demo instance)

docs.title: Official EWP specifications
docs.text:
The EWP network's general documentation and specifications are public and maintained by the consortium — useful for an IT team that wants the schema detail:

  • EWP Developers Guide
  • GitHub organisation — all specifications
  • Architecture & security
  • The mobility process explained
  • Each API's specification lives in an ewp-specs-api-<name> repository, e.g. IIAs · Institutions · Outgoing Mobilities

Note

The API versions listed above match AroundLink's current implementation; if in doubt about a schema, the official specifications prevail.

docs.title: Architecture & technology
docs.text:
Who this page is for

A technical page for IT teams / CIOs (integration, due diligence, operations). It describes the technologies AroundLink is built on, at a product level — with no configuration or secrets.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: AroundLink is a multi-tenant web application (SaaS), built around a Symfony (PHP) core and a PostgreSQL database. The application is API-first: the same business data is exposed through a REST API (see the EWP API reference and the AroundLink REST API), enabling the integrated web interface, decoupled front-ends (React/Next.js) and the machine-to-machine exchanges of the EWP network alike.

docs.title: Application core (backend)
docs.text: Technology Version Role PHP ≥ 8.3 Backend language. Symfony 7.2 Application framework (HTTP, security, forms, validation…). API Platform 4.1 REST API exposure (Hydra / JSON-LD contract, CRUD operations). Doctrine ORM / DBAL 3.x Data access, schema migrations, data sets. Symfony Messenger 7.2 Asynchronous processing (emails, notifications, EWP syncs). Symfony UX (Stimulus) 2.x Browser interactivity without a heavy build (AssetMapper / importmap). Twig 3.x Templates for the integrated interface pages.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL 16. The schema is versioned with Doctrine migrations (reproducible across environments).
  • Public identifiers of sensitive objects use UUIDs (non-guessable / non-enumerable) rather than sequential integers.

docs.title: Interface & front-end components
docs.text:
The integrated interface (institution and student spaces) is rendered with Twig + Stimulus, with:

  • ag-Grid — data grids (sorting, columns, filters, saved views);
  • Chart.js — dashboard charts;
  • Leaflet (+ MarkerCluster, MapTiler basemap) — partner and Atlas directory maps;
  • CKEditor — rich content editing (CMS editor, document templates);
  • autocompletion and live components via Symfony UX.

Front / back separation

The API-first architecture enables a decoupled front-end (a React/Next.js app consuming the API) alongside the existing Twig interface. Both coexist during the transition.

docs.title: Integrations & services
docs.text: Service Use Mailjet Email delivery + tracking (opens, clicks, bounces) for communications and reminders. Gotenberg / mPDF PDF document generation (certificates, agreements, templates). MapTiler (via Leaflet) Basemaps for the Atlas directory. Sentry Application error monitoring. EWP Registry Mirror of the EWP network catalogue (institutions, keys, API versions). spatie/simple-excel Reading CSV / Excel imports (partners, agreements, grants…).

docs.title: Runtime & deployment
docs.text:
• FrankenPHP (a Caddy-based application server) in worker mode: the Symfony kernel stays loaded between requests for better performance.
  • Multi-stage Docker image (reproducible build), boot that waits for the database then applies migrations.
  • Deployable on containerised infrastructure; production is hosted in France, on OVHcloud.
  • Runs behind an HTTPS proxy (trusted proxies configured).

docs.title: Asynchronous processing
docs.text: Tasks that must not block the user (sending emails, notifications, EWP fetches/notifications, grant status updates) go through Symfony Messenger and are processed in the background.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• REST API (API Platform, Hydra / JSON-LD contract) — see the interactive documentation linked from the EWP API reference.
  • EWP API (Erasmus Without Paper network) — endpoints, direction and versions in the same reference.

docs.title: Platform & security
docs.text: AroundLink is a multi-tenant SaaS platform. This page describes the cross-cutting model: data isolation, account types, permissions, sign-in, and commercial plans. The detailed behaviour of each screen lives in the dedicated modules — this page sets the frame.

docs.title: Data isolation (multi-tenancy)
docs.text:
What it is for. Each client institution only ever sees its own data — students, partners, agreements, campaigns, communications, views. One institution's data is never visible to another. This is the platform's fundamental trust guarantee.

Who it is for. All institution-workspace users

How it works. When a coordinator is signed in, the platform automatically restricts everything they see to their own institution. Genuinely shared data (such as the global Atlas directory) is handled separately and clearly identified as such.

Use case.

Two client universities use AroundLink on the same day; neither can see the other's students, agreements or grants.

docs.title: What you write about a partner is yours
docs.text:
What it is for. Separating what describes a partner institution from what you, as a client, have recorded about them. Two institutions can work with the same partner without ever seeing each other's notes.

Who it is for. RI manager / coordinator

How it works. The content you enter about a partner carries your institution's mark and never leaves your workspace:

  • the information you publish to your students about that partner (resources, links, FAQ);
  • the course catalogue you maintain for them;
  • the language scores you declare as a requirement;
  • the files you upload to their record, which keep track of who added them.

Another client working with the same partner keeps their own version of all this, with no interference.

Use case.

Two French institutions send students to the same Spanish university. Each keeps its own course catalogue and its own guidance there, never seeing the other's.

Identity belongs to the institution

A partner's name, country, city, address, email address, website and accreditations can only be edited by that institution itself, from its own workspace. You cannot change them from their record: this identity is unique and serves everyone — search, Atlas, ROR matching, EWP exchanges. What you control on their record is your own layer: your internal code and your tags.

Official identifiers — ROR, Erasmus code, EWP id, SCHAC — cannot be edited by anyone: they are the reference.

docs.title: Account types
docs.text:
What it is for. Three user profiles coexist, each with its own space and permissions, so every actor only sees what concerns them.

Who it is for. IRO coordinator · student · invited partner

How it works. There are:

  • the IRO coordinator (mobility officer) who runs the institution workspace;
  • the student who accesses their personal space;
  • the invited partner — a contact at a partner institution granted access to collaborate (for example, to approve a bilateral agreement).

Use case.

An institution invites a partner's Erasmus officer; they sign in to their own space to approve an agreement, seeing nothing else.

docs.title: Team roles & permissions (RBAC)
docs.text:
What it is for. Within an institution, you can define custom team roles and set, module by module, whether each role has no access, read, or write. This lets a large IRO delegate safely.

Who it is for. IRO coordinator (institution administrator)

How it works. A matrix editor crosses the institution's roles (rows) with the main functional modules (columns) — Institution, Documents, Forms, Workflow, Integrations, Team permissions — each cell being None / Read / Write. Permissions are enforced everywhere: a user without a right neither sees the menu entry nor can reach it via a direct address.

Use case.

The head of the IRO gives the "Assistant" role read access everywhere, but write access only on Documents.

docs.title: Sign-in & single sign-on (SSO)
docs.text:
What it is for. Institutions can let their staff (and students) sign in with their existing Microsoft/Azure institutional account instead of a separate password — and can enforce it. Fewer passwords to manage and compliance with IT requirements.

Who it is for. Configured by the AroundLink team per institution; used by the institution's staff and students

How it works. At sign-in, the platform recognises the institution from the email address entered; if single sign-on is enabled (or enforced), the user is redirected to the Microsoft sign-in page, otherwise they can use a password. Password sign-in also offers standard password reset.

Use case.

A coordinator at an Azure university clicks "Sign in", enters their work email, and is automatically routed to Microsoft authentication.

Are you an IT department?

Protocol, requested permissions, step-by-step onboarding, security checks and known limitations: Microsoft single sign-on (IT).

docs.title: Application access (API key & EWP network)
docs.text:
What it is for. Machine-access channels, separate from the user session, let you connect AroundLink to external systems and authenticate exchanges with partner universities on the EWP network.

Who it is for. IT / integrations · partner university systems

How it works. Each institution has a regenerable API key (managed in Settings) for its integrations, plus dedicated authentication for the EWP network. These machine accesses are deliberately distinct from browser sign-in. The REST API has interactive documentation (resources, schemas, operations) — see the API documentation (demo) and, for the EWP network, the EWP API reference.

docs.title: Plans: paid / free institution
docs.text:
What it is for. Each institution is either a paying or a free client; some premium modules (for example mobility grants or creating bilateral agreements) are reserved to paying clients. This is the platform's commercial gating.

Who it is for. Client institution (set by AroundLink)

How it works. The institution's plan (paid by default, or free) governs access to premium modules — hidden in the menu and blocked on direct access for a free client. This plan is independent of any tuition fees paid by the student.

Use case.

A free-plan partner can review and approve a bilateral agreement a paying institution submitted to it, but cannot open premium modules.

docs.title: Contextual help
docs.text:
What it is for. Give every screen its own instructions, without leaving the page or hunting through separate documentation.

Who it is for. every signed-in user

How it works. A "?" button sits at the top right of every page. It opens a panel explaining what you can do here, in French and in English, sometimes with a short video. The panel closes as soon as you change page: what you read always matches the screen in front of you.

Each text ends with a booking link: if the explanation is not enough, you book a fifteen-minute slot with the AroundLink team.

Use case.

A new team member opens the place-distribution screen, clicks "?", understands how the grid works, and fills it in without having to ask.

docs.title: Service marketplace
docs.text:
What it is for. A catalog of third-party services (insurance, housing, banking…) that can be shown to students, switchable on per institution. A value-add space, shown only where it is enabled.

Who it is for. Student (browsing) · AroundLink (curation)

How it works. The catalog of providers and offers is maintained by AroundLink; a per-institution switch decides whether the marketplace appears to that institution's students. When on, students see the offers in their Services space, sorted by category and saveable to their favourites. An institution can individually set aside an offer it does not want shown to its students. This is display + affiliation (links and promo codes to the provider): no payment goes through AroundLink — the student subscribes on the partner's site.

Use case.

AroundLink adds a "Student health insurance — from €9/month" offer; it appears to students of marketplace-enabled institutions.

docs.title: Security & data
docs.text:
Who this page is for

A technical page for CIOs / CISOs evaluating AroundLink. It describes the security measures at a product level. It deliberately contains no configuration detail, secret or exploitable element. More detailed security documentation can be provided on request in an appropriate setting.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
• Microsoft / Azure SSO (OpenID Connect) — institutions can let their users sign in with their existing institutional account; single sign-on can be enforced per institution, with allowed email domains. Onboarding procedure, requested permissions and checks performed: Microsoft single sign-on (IT).
  • Password sign-in (when SSO is not enforced) — passwords are hashed (never stored in clear text), with a strength check at creation and reset via a single-use, time-limited link.
  • Rate limiting on sign-in and reset attempts, to slow down brute-force attacks.

docs.title: Authorisation & isolation
docs.text:
• Multi-tenant isolation — every query is automatically restricted to the data of the signed-in user's institution; one institution never sees another's data.
  • Roles & permissions (RBAC) — per-module rights (none / read / write), enforced server-side (hiding a menu is not enough: direct access is blocked too). See the Overview.
  • Ownership checks on objects accessed by identifier, on top of tenant isolation, to prevent access to someone else's resource.

docs.title: API & network
docs.text:
• Application API — authentication via JWT token (RSA-key signed) and regenerable API keys, on a channel separate from the browser session.
  • EWP network — every incoming and outgoing exchange is signed and verified (RSA HTTP signatures, the EWP standard); the caller is identified by its public key declared in the EWP Registry, which governs data access.

docs.title: Data protection
docs.text:
• Encryption in transit — the application runs behind HTTPS (trusted proxies configured).
  • Non-enumerable identifiers — sensitive objects (placements, agreements, student files…) are referenced by UUID.
  • CSRF protection on forms and sensitive actions.
  • Validated-document locking — a validated document can no longer be altered or deleted on the student side.
  • Minimisation — only the data needed for the mobility process is collected; students' personal data (identity, contact details, grades) is handled solely in that context.

docs.title: Monitoring & continuity
docs.text:
• Application error monitoring (Sentry) to detect and diagnose incidents.
  • Database backups on demand, with retention and download, from the admin console.
  • Logging & history — key decisions (document validations, agreement changes, nomination decisions) keep a timestamped history with the author.

docs.title: Compliance & hosting
docs.text:
• AroundLink operates within the Erasmus+ / EWP framework, the European mobility interoperability standard.
  • Production is hosted in France, on OVHcloud — a French provider, subject to French and European law. Students' personal data never leaves the European Union, in line with GDPR for students' personal data.

Note

This page is an overview. For a security questionnaire, an audit or contractual details, contact the AroundLink team.

docs.title: Microsoft sign-in
docs.text:
Your users — staff and students alike — can sign in to AroundLink with their Microsoft account, work or personal, with no extra password to remember.

Since September 2026, there is nothing to configure in the common case. Each person links their own account, in two clicks, from their profile.

docs.title: The common case: everyone links their own account
docs.text:
What it's for. Signing in with one click, no password, no request to your IT department or to us.

Who it's for. every AroundLink user

How it works. In three steps.

  1. The user signs in to AroundLink with their password, as usual.
  2. From their profile, they link their Microsoft account — work or personal.
  3. From then on, the "Sign in with Microsoft" button on the home page lets them straight in.

They can unlink it whenever they want and go back to signing in with their password.

A matching email address is never enough

Sign-in recognises the linked Microsoft account, not the address it carries. Someone turning up with a Microsoft account bearing the same email as one of your users would not get in: they would see "This Microsoft account is not linked to any AroundLink account. Sign in with your password, then link it from your profile."

That is what makes it safe to open Microsoft sign-in to everyone without checking anything upfront.

The messages your users may see:

Message What it means This Microsoft account is not linked to any AroundLink account They must sign in with their password first and link their account This Microsoft account is already linked to another AroundLink account A Microsoft account can serve only one AroundLink identity This account signs in with Microsoft — there is no password to set The account was created under forced SSO, with no password

Use case.

A coordinator has had enough of remembering one more password. She signs in, opens her profile, links her school account, and signs in with one click from that day on — without having had to ask anyone for anything.

docs.title: The forced-SSO case
docs.text:
What it's for. Making Microsoft sign-in the only way in for your institution — no passwords to manage, and leavers handled in your directory, not with us.

Who it's for. IT department

How it works. This is the only case that calls for an exchange with our team. Your users then have nothing to link: linking happens at their first sign-in, automatically, from their email address.

docs.title: What we need from you
docs.text: What Where to find it 1 Your Microsoft tenant identifier Microsoft Entra portal ▸ Overview ▸ Tenant ID 2 The list of your allowed email domains Only you know it

docs.title: What we do next
docs.text:
We record your configuration and enable it. From then on, anyone from your institution arriving with an address on an allowed domain is linked to their AroundLink account at first sign-in.

Allowed domains are not optional

An enabled configuration must declare at least one domain. With no domain, nobody is linked at first sign-in — and since forced SSO removes the password, your users would be locked out. The platform therefore refuses an enabled configuration with no domain.

Accounts must exist beforehand

Single sign-on verifies who you are. It does not decide that you are allowed in. A user who does not yet exist in AroundLink will be refused, even with a perfectly valid Microsoft account. Create or import your accounts before enabling.

Use case.

The university mandates its directory for every tool. Its IT department sends us the tenant identifier and two domains. We enable it. The two hundred accounts already in AroundLink link themselves over the first few sign-ins, with nobody having to do anything.

docs.title: What we read from your directory
docs.text: Data read name, email address, Microsoft account identifier Data not requested mail, files, calendar, directory, groups, memberships Passwords never pass through AroundLink Application to declare on your side none Scope institution staff and students

docs.title: Single sign-on (IT departments)
docs.text:
Who this page is for

This page is technical: it addresses IT departments and infrastructure teams who want to know how their users sign in to AroundLink. For the business value, see the Overview.

AroundLink users — international office staff and students alike — can sign in with their institutional account, with no extra password to create or manage.

The connection is configured per institution. Each one picks its mode: single sign-on alone, or single sign-on alongside passwords during the transition.

docs.title: Identity providers
docs.text:
Provider Status Guide Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) ✅ Available Onboarding guide Shibboleth / SAML 2.0 (RENATER, eduGAIN, SWITCHaai…) 🗺️ On the roadmap — Google Workspace 🗺️ On the roadmap —

Roadmap

Microsoft Entra ID is the provider you can connect today. Academic identity federation (Shibboleth / SAML, RENATER, eduGAIN) and Google Workspace are on our roadmap, with no announced date at this stage.

If your institution authenticates through one of those, do tell us: what institutions ask for decides the order in which we open them. In the meantime, password sign-in remains available, with single-use reset links — see Security & data.

The sign-in screen: the password, and "Sign in with Microsoft", offered to everyone at all times. There is no account creation — access is opened by the international office.

docs.title: What holds for every provider
docs.text: The following does not depend on the protocol. It holds for Microsoft today, and will hold for the providers we add.

docs.title: Accounts must exist beforehand
docs.text:
The prerequisite most often discovered too late

Single sign-on connects accounts, it does not create them. A user who is absent from AroundLink is refused entry, even with a perfectly valid institutional account.

Accounts are created beforehand by the institution: importing the student list, or creation by the international office. See Settings & team.

There is no directory synchronisation (no SCIM) and no group or role synchronisation: AroundLink permissions are granted inside AroundLink.

docs.title: The sign-in journey
docs.text:
The "Sign in with Microsoft" button sits on the home page, for everyone, permanently. There is nothing to look for and nothing to declare upfront.

What happens next depends on one thing only: is the Microsoft account linked to an AroundLink account?

  1. Yes — the user gets in. Your directory's rules apply along the way (password, multi-factor, conditional access): they are yours, not ours.
  2. No — entry is refused, with the explanation: sign in with a password first, then link the account from your profile.

Recognition is on the linked account, never on the email address alone. That is what makes it safe to open Microsoft sign-in to everyone with no upfront check.

docs.title: Settings, per institution
docs.text:
In the common case there are no settings: each person links their own account. The settings below concern only institutions that want to mandate single sign-on.

Setting Effect Enable Your users are linked automatically at first sign-in, from their address. Strict mode Removes password sign-in: your directory becomes the only way in. Allowed email domains The domains whose addresses trigger that automatic linking. Required as soon as you enable.

Why domains are required

With no domain declared, nobody is linked at first sign-in. Combined with strict mode, which removes the password, your users would be locked out. The platform therefore refuses an enabled configuration with no domain.

Do not turn on strict mode first

Strict mode removes the password fallback. Turn it on only after checking that at least one account really gets in through single sign-on.

docs.title: Leavers and joiners
docs.text: Event on your side Effect in AroundLink Institutional account disabled (leaver) The person can no longer sign in, immediately. Authentication rules changed (MFA, password) Nothing to do in AroundLink: those rules are yours. New joiner Their AroundLink account must be created first.

docs.title: AroundLink administration accounts
docs.text:
The vendor's internal accounts never sign in through a customer's single sign-on, by design.

See also: Microsoft Entra ID — onboarding guide · Security & data · Platform overview

docs.title: Cuando algo no funciona
docs.text: Las situaciones que se encuentran de verdad, con su causa y qué hacer. Casi todas tienen el mismo origen: una condición fijada antes no se cumple, y la pantalla se niega en lugar de adivinar.

docs.title: «No veo ninguna campaña»
docs.text:
Tres causas posibles, en este orden de frecuencia.

La campaña no está abierta. Solo el estado Abierta acepta preferencias. Una campaña «Lista» es visible para usted, no para sus estudiantes.

El estudiante no forma parte del grupo. Los criterios de la campaña — nivel, itinerario, campus, etiquetas, filtros — no lo retienen. Abra la campaña y mire la lista de participantes: si no está, añádalo a mano.

El estudiante no tiene perfil. Sin expediente, no existe para ninguna campaña.

docs.title: «No puedo validar mis preferencias»
docs.text: Usted ha fijado un mínimo de preferencias y no lo ha alcanzado. El mínimo bloquea tanto como el máximo.

docs.title: «No encuentro ningún destino»
docs.text:
El grupo de destinos de la campaña está vacío, o no hay ninguna plaza colocada en los acuerdos que retiene. Compruebe la matriz de plazas antes de buscar en otra parte: un destino sin plaza no se muestra.

Compruebe también el periodo: una plaza existe siempre para un periodo dado.

docs.title: «Ya no veo mi clasificación»
docs.text: Es intencionado, si su institución ha ocultado la clasificación a los estudiantes. El ajuste está en Lo que ven sus estudiantes — usted y su equipo siguen viéndola.

docs.title: «No he recibido mis accesos»
docs.text: Un acceso abierto no es un acceso recibido. Mire la columna de estado del acceso en su lista de estudiantes: dice si ha salido y cuándo. Y la columna Connected dice si ya se ha conectado — son dos preguntas distintas.

docs.title: «La ronda de asignación se niega a arrancar»
docs.text:
Es el bloqueo más frecuente, y siempre viene explicado: el informe nombra a los estudiantes que bloquean y la razón.

Mensaje Qué hacer El estudiante no tiene itinerario Asígnele uno. Si su institución no los usa, cree uno por nivel. El estudiante no tiene clasificación Importe la clasificación antes de relanzar. La ronda no la fabrica. El estudiante no tiene perfil No hay nada que colocar. Su expediente está incompleto Complételo, o ajuste la campaña a «señalar» en vez de «bloquear».

La ronda no es un gesto único

Corrija lo que bloquea y relánsela tantas veces como haga falta.

docs.title: «No puedo eliminar esta campaña»
docs.text: Solo se elimina una campaña en borrador. Una campaña abierta ya lleva preferencias.

docs.title: «No puedo reabrir esta campaña»
docs.text: Solo se reabre una campaña terminada. Y si la reabre sin aplazar su fecha de fin, volverá a cerrarse a la mañana siguiente.

docs.title: «Mi campaña se ha cerrado sola»
docs.text: Su fecha de fin ha pasado. Es el funcionamiento normal desde septiembre de 2026: al día siguiente del último día, la campaña se cierra, las preferencias en borrador se convierten en preferencias y usted recibe el balance. Reábrala y aplace la fecha si era prematuro.

docs.title: «Mis contadores de plazas no dicen lo mismo que mi exportación»
docs.text: Desde septiembre de 2026, todos los contadores de plazas cubren únicamente las movilidades salientes — las que usted envía. Las plazas que sus socios abren en su casa ya no inflan sus totales. Si una cifra le sorprende, probablemente era falsa antes.

docs.title: «No puedo recordárselo a este socio»
docs.text: Un recordatorio cada veinticuatro horas. El botón se desactiva después, y le dirá cuándo.

docs.title: «No puedo nominar a este estudiante en este acuerdo»
docs.text: Ya hay una nominación en curso en ese acuerdo para él. Retírela primero si quiere rehacerla.

docs.title: «Este socio no aparece en mi campaña»
docs.text: El grupo de destinos no lo retiene: compruebe los tipos de acuerdo, los periodos y los filtros de institución de la campaña. Compruebe también que no esté archivado ni oculto.

docs.title: «No puedo rechazar esta nominación»
docs.text: Un rechazo exige un motivo. Se transmitirá a la institución que le nominó al estudiante.

docs.title: Del lado de accesos y permisos
«Esta pantalla es de solo lectura»
docs.text: Su rol le da el nivel Consultar en esta sección. Un banner lo indica en la parte superior. Su pantalla Mis permisos le dice exactamente qué puede hacer y sobre quién.

docs.title: «Este estudiante está fuera de mi perímetro»
docs.text: Su rol se limita a una dirección, un campus o unas promociones que no lo cubren. No es una avería: es el perímetro definido por su administrador.

docs.title: «Parte de mi selección no se ha procesado»
docs.text: Su acción afectaba a filas fuera de su perímetro. Se apartan, y la pantalla le dice cuáles.

docs.title: «No puedo conectarme con mi cuenta de la institución»
docs.text: El inicio de sesión único verifica quién es usted, no decide que tenga derecho a entrar. Su cuenta debe existir previamente en AroundLink. Véase Quién aporta qué.

docs.title: «No puedo guardar este resultado de idioma»
docs.text: Un resultado exige siempre un justificante. El archivo y la fecha son obligatorios.

docs.title: «Me piden un motivo para modificar el contrato de estudios»
docs.text: Todo componente añadido o retirado tras la validación exige una justificación. Es una exigencia del contrato, no un ajuste.

docs.title: Documentación de producto AroundLink
docs.text:
AroundLink es la plataforma de gestión de la movilidad estudiantil internacional (Erasmus+ / EWP) para las oficinas de relaciones internacionales de escuelas y universidades. Reúne en un mismo lugar los socios, los acuerdos, las campañas de candidatura, los documentos contractuales, las becas y el intercambio de datos con la red europea — para sustituir las hojas de cálculo y los correos dispersos por un proceso único, trazable y conforme.

Esta documentación recoge todas las funcionalidades de la herramienta y, para cada una, su valor para su trabajo. Está dirigida a usted:

  • Responsables y gestores de relaciones internacionales: entender qué hace la herramienta y qué aporta, sin jerga técnica.
  • Departamentos de informática: las páginas de Plataforma responden a las preguntas de conexión, autenticación e intercambio de datos.

Cómo leer una ficha

Cada funcionalidad sigue el mismo formato: para qué sirve, para quién, cómo funciona, y un caso de uso concreto. Los recuadros señalan lo que conviene saber antes de activar un ajuste, y las trampas que solo se ven una vez dentro.

Direcciones útiles

La aplicación: app.aroundlink.com — ahí es donde trabaja cada día.

El sitio AroundLink: aroundlink.com — la presentación del producto, y la forma de contactarnos.

Esta documentación describe lo que hace la herramienta; no sustituye a la aplicación.

docs.title: Los tres espacios
docs.text:
• Espacio institución

    El espacio de trabajo de la oficina: socios y acuerdos, campañas de movilidad, documentos (Learning Agreement, expedientes de notas), becas Erasmus+, comunicaciones y seguimiento.

    Panel de control

  • Portal del estudiante

    El recorrido del estudiante, desde el descubrimiento de destinos hasta la candidatura, y después durante y tras la movilidad (contrato de estudios, certificados, expediente de notas).

    Descubrir & solicitar

  • Atlas & red EWP

    El directorio mundial de instituciones y la integración con la red Erasmus Without Paper para intercambiar acuerdos, contratos y expedientes sin papel.

    Atlas · EWP

docs.title: Una palabra sobre el multi-institución
docs.text: AroundLink es una plataforma multi-institución (SaaS): cada institución cliente ve únicamente sus propios datos (estudiantes, acuerdos, campañas…), totalmente aislados de los de las demás. Coexisten tres tipos de cuenta — coordinador de relaciones internacionales, estudiante y socio invitado — cada uno con su espacio y sus permisos. Véase Plataforma y seguridad.

docs.title: Índice
docs.text:
• Espacio institución — socios, acuerdos, campañas, documentos, becas, comunicaciones, ajustes.
  • Portal del estudiante — perfil, búsqueda, candidatura, movilidad, contrato de estudios, expediente de notas.
  • Atlas — Directorio mundial — el directorio de instituciones de todo el mundo.
  • Red EWP — el intercambio de datos con las universidades socias.
  • Plataforma y seguridad — cuentas, roles, SSO, planes.
  • Glosario — EWP, IIA, OLA, ToR, EQF, ISCED…

docs.title: Una movilidad de principio a fin
Una movilidad de principio a fin
docs.text:
Esta página sigue una movilidad completa, desde el primer ajuste hasta el expediente de notas, indicando en cada etapa quién actúa y qué desencadena la siguiente.

El resto de la documentación describe las pantallas una por una. Esta describe el encadenamiento — que suele ser lo que falta cuando uno busca por qué un expediente no avanza.

docs.title: Antes de cualquier campaña: el terreno
docs.text:
Nada de lo que sigue funciona si estas cuatro cosas no existen.

Lo que hace falta Quién lo prepara Si falta Sus socios y sus acuerdos Coordinador Ningún destino que ofrecer Plazas colocadas en la matriz Coordinador Los destinos existen pero no abren nada Sus itinerarios (uno por promoción, o uno por nivel) Administrador, en los ajustes La ronda de asignación se niega a arrancar Sus periodos de movilidad Administrador Las plazas no tienen columna donde colocarse

El error de arranque más frecuente

Crear una campaña antes de haber colocado plazas. La campaña se abre, los estudiantes la ven, y no encuentran ningún destino. Compruebe la matriz antes de abrir.

docs.title: 1. La campaña se abre
docs.text:
Quién actúa: el coordinador.

Crea la campaña, elige quién participa y adónde se puede ir, fija el número de preferencias, los documentos exigidos y las pocas opciones que luego no se pueden rehacer. Véase Configurar una campaña, ajuste por ajuste.

La campaña pasa de Borrador a Lista, y después a Abierta.

Qué desencadena lo siguiente: solo el estado Abierta acepta preferencias. Una campaña «Lista» se mira, no se rellena.

docs.title: 2. El estudiante registra sus preferencias
docs.text:
Quién actúa: el estudiante.

Descubre los destinos, guarda algunos como favoritos, y registra sus preferencias desde la misma pantalla donde los descubre. Las ordena por orden de prioridad.

Si usted ha fijado un mínimo de preferencias, no puede validar hasta alcanzarlo. Si ha activado la respuesta «no deseo irme», también puede declararlo — sin tener que justificarse.

Qué desencadena lo siguiente: el cierre de la campaña, en su fecha de fin o por usted. Las preferencias aún en borrador se convierten entonces en preferencias reales.

docs.title: 3. La asignación
docs.text:
Quién actúa: el coordinador.

Dos caminos, que coexisten.

La ronda automática atiende a los estudiantes por orden de clasificación: el primero obtiene su mejor preferencia disponible, y lo que queda pasa al siguiente. Exige de cada participante un perfil, un itinerario y una clasificación importada — véase Lo que exige el emparejamiento. Puede relanzarse tantas veces como sea necesario.

La asignación manual no está limitada por nada. Coloca a quien quiera, donde quiera, clasificado o no.

Qué desencadena lo siguiente: existe una asignación.

docs.title: 4. El estudiante acepta — o no
docs.text:
Quién actúa: el estudiante, salvo si usted ha elegido la asignación directa.

Recibe su propuesta y la acepta o la rechaza. Si ha configurado la campaña en asignación directa, esta etapa desaparece: su decisión crea la asignación.

Qué desencadena lo siguiente: la aceptación.

docs.title: 5. La nominación ante el socio
docs.text:
Quién actúa: el coordinador, y después la institución de acogida.

Usted nomina al estudiante ante su destino. El socio recibe la información y responde — por la plataforma, por la red EWP, por correo o por teléfono. Usted registra su respuesta indicando por qué canal llegó.

Mientras no haya respondido, puede recordárselo (una vez cada veinticuatro horas) o retirar la nominación, lo que deja al estudiante disponible para otro destino.

Un rechazo va siempre acompañado de un motivo, transmitido a la institución que nominó.

Qué desencadena lo siguiente: la confirmación del socio.

docs.title: 6. El expediente se completa
docs.text:
Quién actúa: el estudiante aporta, el coordinador valida.

Documentos contractuales, resultados de idiomas, contrato de estudios. Cada pieza esperada está listada, y el estudiante ve lo que le falta. Usted recuerda a los rezagados desde la barra de selección de su lista, sin llevar una lista aparte.

Según el ajuste de la campaña, un expediente incompleto bloquea la asignación o simplemente se señala.

Qué desencadena lo siguiente: el expediente está completo y se acercan las fechas.

docs.title: 7. La salida, y después la estancia
docs.text:
Quién actúa: todos, poco a poco.

El estudiante se marcha. Su contrato de estudios puede modificarse por el camino — todo cambio de componente exige un motivo. Los vencimientos del periodo aparecen en la agenda, y en el calendario al que cada uno se haya suscrito.

docs.title: 8. El regreso
docs.text:
Quién actúa: la institución de acogida, y después el estudiante.

La institución que ha acogido introduce las notas en su propia escala y emite el expediente de notas; el estudiante recibe aviso y lo encuentra en su ficha.

El estudiante deja su valoración sobre la institución de acogida — y puede autorizar la publicación de sus fotos. A quienes no han respondido se les recuerda como con los documentos.

Qué cierra el círculo: la valoración alimenta la ficha del socio, que los siguientes estudiantes leerán antes de elegir sus preferencias.

docs.title: Agenda
docs.text:
La agenda reúne todas las fechas de su institución en un mismo lugar: semestres, campañas, vencimientos de sus socios, etapas de acogida, nominaciones y eventos.

Hasta ahora esas fechas vivían en cinco pantallas distintas, y nadie podía responder sin más a «¿qué vence el mes que viene?».

docs.title: Lo que encuentra ahí
docs.text:
Para qué sirve. Anticiparse. Un vencimiento de nominación, el cierre de una campaña y el inicio de curso de un socio no son del mismo orden, pero caen en el mismo mes, y eso es lo que cuenta al organizar el trabajo.

Para quién. todo el equipo de movilidad

Cómo funciona. La agenda no inventa ninguna fecha y no modifica ninguna: reúne lo que ya existe en otra parte. Cada entrada remite al objeto del que procede, y es ahí donde la fecha se modifica — de lo contrario dos versiones del mismo vencimiento acabarían por contradecirse.

Alterna entre una vista de lista y una vista de mes, y filtra por:

  • la familia — Semestres, Campañas, Socios, Nominación, Acogida, Aplicación, Otros;
  • la dirección — salientes o entrantes;
  • solo su equipo, para apartar lo que no le concierne.

Los filtros se acumulan, y la barra de filtros permanece a la vista mientras la lista se desplaza.

También puede añadir una fecha a mano, para lo que no existe en ningún otro sitio: una reunión de comisión, un plazo interno.

El mes en curso, cada fecha con el color de su familia. Arriba, los filtros que se acumulan y el botón de suscripción a su calendario.

docs.title: Recuperar sus fechas en Outlook
docs.text:
Para qué sirve. Consultar las fechas de AroundLink desde el calendario que ya utiliza, sin abrir la herramienta.

Para quién. todo el equipo de movilidad, y sus estudiantes

Cómo funciona. AroundLink publica su agenda en el formato estándar que todos los calendarios saben leer desde hace veinte años. Copia la dirección de suscripción, la pega en Outlook, y sus fechas aparecen — actualizándose solas a partir de ahí.

No es una integración con Microsoft: es un formato abierto. Outlook, Google Calendar, Apple Calendario y los demás se sirven igual, y su departamento de informática no tiene nada que autorizar ni configurar.

La sincronización va en un solo sentido

Su calendario viene a leer las fechas de AroundLink. No las modifica: un vencimiento de nominación no debe poder moverse desde el Outlook de un estudiante. Para cambiar una fecha, pase por la pantalla de la que procede.

Se suscribe a lo que está mirando. La dirección recoge los filtros mostrados en el momento en que la copia. Puede así crear varias suscripciones — «mis nominaciones» por un lado, «los eventos del equipo» por otro — y verlas como dos calendarios distintos en Outlook, que muestra u oculta por separado.

Lo que contiene el flujo. Únicamente fechas y su título. Ningún nombre de estudiante, ningún dato personal circula por este canal.

Caso de uso.

La coordinadora se suscribe a la agenda de su equipo filtrada por salientes. Cada lunes ve en su Outlook los vencimientos de la semana sin abrir AroundLink. Cuando una fecha cambia en la herramienta, su calendario la sigue.

La dirección de suscripción es personal

Da acceso a su agenda, y solo a la suya. No la transmita: quien la reciba vería sus fechas. Cada persona crea la suya desde su propia cuenta.

docs.title: Quando qualcosa non funziona
docs.text: Le situazioni che si incontrano davvero, con la loro causa e cosa fare. Quasi tutte hanno la stessa origine: una condizione posta a monte non è soddisfatta, e la schermata rifiuta invece di indovinare.

docs.title: «Non vedo nessuna campagna»
docs.text:
Tre cause possibili, in quest'ordine di frequenza.

La campagna non è aperta. Solo lo stato Aperta accetta preferenze. Una campagna «Pronta» è visibile a voi, non ai vostri studenti.

Lo studente non fa parte del bacino. I criteri della campagna — livello, percorso, campus, etichette, filtri — non lo trattengono. Aprite la campagna e guardate l'elenco dei partecipanti: se non c'è, aggiungetelo a mano.

Lo studente non ha un profilo. Senza pratica, non esiste per nessuna campagna.

docs.title: «Non riesco a convalidare le mie preferenze»
docs.text: Avete fissato un minimo di preferenze e non l'ha raggiunto. Il minimo blocca quanto il massimo.

docs.title: «Non trovo nessuna destinazione»
docs.text:
Il bacino di destinazioni della campagna è vuoto, oppure nessun posto è collocato sugli accordi che trattiene. Verificate la matrice dei posti prima di cercare altrove: una destinazione senza posti non compare.

Verificate anche il periodo: un posto esiste sempre per un periodo dato.

docs.title: «Non vedo più la mia classifica»
docs.text: È voluto, se il vostro istituto ha nascosto la classifica agli studenti. L'impostazione è in Cosa vedono i vostri studenti — voi e il vostro team continuate a vederla.

docs.title: «Non ho ricevuto i miei accessi»
docs.text: Un accesso aperto non è un accesso ricevuto. Guardate la colonna di stato dell'accesso nel vostro elenco studenti: dice se è partito e quando. E la colonna Connected dice se si è già collegato — sono due domande diverse.

docs.title: «Il turno di assegnazione si rifiuta di partire»
docs.text:
È il blocco più frequente, ed è sempre spiegato: il resoconto nomina gli studenti che bloccano e la ragione.

Messaggio Cosa fare Lo studente non ha percorso Collegatelo a un percorso. Se il vostro istituto non ne usa, createne uno per livello. Lo studente non ha classifica Importate la classifica prima di rilanciare. Il turno non la fabbrica. Lo studente non ha profilo Non c'è nulla da collocare. La sua pratica è incompleta Completatela, o impostate la campagna su «segnalare» anziché «bloccare».

Il turno non è un gesto unico

Correggete ciò che blocca e rilanciatelo tutte le volte che serve.

docs.title: «Non riesco a eliminare questa campagna»
docs.text: Si elimina solo una campagna in bozza. Una campagna aperta porta già delle preferenze.

docs.title: «Non riesco a riaprire questa campagna»
docs.text: Si riapre solo una campagna terminata. E se la riaprite senza spostare la data di fine, si richiuderà già il mattino dopo.

docs.title: «La mia campagna si è chiusa da sola»
docs.text: La sua data di fine è passata. È il funzionamento normale da settembre 2026: il giorno dopo l'ultimo giorno la campagna si chiude, le preferenze in bozza diventano preferenze e voi ricevete il bilancio. Riapritela e spostate la data se era prematuro.

docs.title: «I miei contatori dei posti non dicono la stessa cosa dell'esportazione»
docs.text: Da settembre 2026, tutti i contatori dei posti riguardano solo le mobilità in uscita — quelle che inviate voi. I posti che i vostri partner aprono da loro non gonfiano più i vostri totali. Se una cifra vi sorprende, probabilmente era sbagliata prima.

docs.title: «Non riesco a sollecitare questo partner»
docs.text: Una sollecitazione ogni ventiquattro ore. Il pulsante si disattiva dopo, e vi dirà quando.

docs.title: «Non riesco a nominare questo studente su questo accordo»
docs.text: C'è già una nomina in corso su quell'accordo per lui. Ritiratela prima, se volete rifarla.

docs.title: «Questo partner non compare nella mia campagna»
docs.text: Il bacino di destinazioni non lo trattiene: verificate i tipi di accordo, i periodi e i filtri di istituto della campagna. Verificate anche che non sia archiviato o nascosto.

docs.title: «Non riesco a rifiutare questa nomina»
docs.text: Un rifiuto richiede un motivo. Sarà trasmesso all'istituto che vi ha nominato lo studente.

docs.title: «Questa schermata è in sola lettura»
docs.text: Il vostro ruolo vi dà il livello Consultare su questa sezione. Un banner lo dice in alto. La vostra schermata I miei permessi vi dice esattamente cosa potete fare e su chi.

docs.title: «Questo studente è fuori dal mio perimetro»
docs.text: Il vostro ruolo è limitato a una direzione, un campus o delle coorti che non lo coprono. Non è un guasto: è il perimetro definito dal vostro amministratore.

docs.title: «Una parte della mia selezione non è stata trattata»
docs.text: La vostra azione riguardava righe fuori dal vostro perimetro. Vengono messe da parte, e la schermata vi dice quali.

docs.title: «Non riesco ad accedere con l'account del mio istituto»
docs.text: Il single sign-on verifica chi siete, non decide che avete il diritto di entrare. Il vostro account deve esistere già in AroundLink. Si veda Chi fornisce cosa.

docs.title: «Non riesco a salvare questo punteggio linguistico»
docs.text: Un punteggio richiede sempre un giustificativo. Il file e la data sono obbligatori.

docs.title: «Mi viene chiesto un motivo per modificare il learning agreement»
docs.text: Ogni componente aggiunto o rimosso dopo la convalida richiede una giustificazione. È un'esigenza del contratto, non un'impostazione.

docs.title: Documentazione di prodotto AroundLink
docs.text:
AroundLink è la piattaforma di gestione della mobilità studentesca internazionale (Erasmus+ / EWP) per gli uffici relazioni internazionali di scuole e università. Riunisce in un unico luogo i partner, gli accordi, le campagne di candidatura, i documenti contrattuali, le borse e lo scambio di dati con la rete europea — per sostituire fogli di calcolo e e-mail sparse con un processo unico, tracciabile e conforme.

Questa documentazione raccoglie tutte le funzionalità dello strumento e, per ciascuna, il suo valore per il vostro lavoro. Si rivolge a voi:

  • Responsabili e gestori delle relazioni internazionali: capire cosa fa lo strumento e cosa porta, senza gergo tecnico.
  • Servizi informatici: le pagine Piattaforma rispondono alle domande di collegamento, autenticazione e scambio di dati.

Come leggere una scheda

Ogni funzionalità segue lo stesso formato: a cosa serve, per chi, come funziona, e un caso d'uso concreto. I riquadri segnalano ciò che conviene sapere prima di attivare un'impostazione, e le trappole che si vedono solo una volta dentro.

Indirizzi utili

L'applicazione: app.aroundlink.com — è lì che lavorate ogni giorno.

Il sito AroundLink: aroundlink.com — la presentazione del prodotto, e il modo per contattarci.

Questa documentazione descrive cosa fa lo strumento; non sostituisce l'applicazione.

docs.title: I tre spazi
docs.text:
• Spazio istituzione

    Lo spazio di lavoro dell'ufficio: partner e accordi, campagne di mobilità, documenti (Learning Agreement, transcript), borse Erasmus+, comunicazioni e monitoraggio.

    Cruscotto

  • Portale studente

    Il percorso dello studente, dalla scoperta delle destinazioni alla candidatura, e poi durante e dopo la mobilità (learning agreement, attestati, transcript).

    Scoprire & candidarsi

  • Atlas & rete EWP

    La directory mondiale degli istituti e l'integrazione con la rete Erasmus Without Paper per scambiare accordi, contratti e transcript senza carta.

    Atlas · EWP

docs.title: Una parola sul multi-istituzione
docs.text: AroundLink è una piattaforma multi-istituzione (SaaS): ogni istituzione cliente vede soltanto i propri dati (studenti, accordi, campagne…), completamente isolati da quelli delle altre. Coesistono tre tipi di account — coordinatore relazioni internazionali, studente e partner invitato — ciascuno con il proprio spazio e i propri permessi. Si veda Piattaforma e sicurezza.

docs.title: Indice
docs.text:
• Spazio istituzione — partner, accordi, campagne, documenti, borse, comunicazioni, impostazioni.
  • Portale studente — profilo, ricerca, candidatura, mobilità, learning agreement, transcript.
  • Atlas — Directory mondiale — la directory degli istituti di tutto il mondo.
  • Rete EWP — lo scambio di dati con le università partner.
  • Piattaforma e sicurezza — account, ruoli, SSO, piani.
  • Glossario — EWP, IIA, OLA, ToR, EQF, ISCED…

docs.title: Una mobilità dall'inizio alla fine
docs.text:
Questa pagina segue un'intera mobilità, dalla prima impostazione fino al transcript, indicando a ogni tappa chi agisce e cosa innesca la successiva.

Il resto della documentazione descrive le schermate una per una. Questa descrive la concatenazione — spesso ciò che manca quando si cerca perché una pratica non avanza.

docs.title: Prima di ogni campagna: il terreno
docs.text:
Nulla di quanto segue funziona se queste quattro cose non esistono.

Cosa serve Chi lo prepara In sua assenza I vostri partner e i loro accordi Coordinatore Nessuna destinazione da proporre Posti collocati nella matrice Coordinatore Le destinazioni esistono ma non aprono nulla I vostri percorsi (uno per coorte, o uno per livello) Amministratore, nelle impostazioni Il turno di assegnazione si rifiuta di partire I vostri periodi di mobilità Amministratore I posti non hanno una colonna in cui collocarsi

L'errore di avvio più frequente

Creare una campagna prima di aver collocato dei posti. La campagna si apre, gli studenti la vedono, e non trovano alcuna destinazione. Verificate la matrice prima di aprire.

docs.title: 1. La campagna si apre
docs.text:
Chi agisce: il coordinatore.

Crea la campagna, sceglie chi partecipa e dove si può andare, imposta il numero di preferenze, i documenti richiesti e le poche opzioni che poi non si possono rifare. Si veda Configurare una campagna, impostazione per impostazione.

La campagna passa da Bozza a Pronta, poi ad Aperta.

Cosa innesca il seguito: solo lo stato Aperta accetta preferenze. Una campagna «Pronta» si guarda, non si riempie.

docs.title: 2. Lo studente deposita le sue preferenze
docs.text:
Chi agisce: lo studente.

Scopre le destinazioni, ne mette da parte alcune tra i preferiti, e deposita le sue preferenze dalla stessa schermata in cui le scopre. Le ordina per preferenza.

Se avete fissato un minimo di preferenze, non può convalidare finché non lo raggiunge. Se avete attivato la risposta «non desidero partire», può anche dichiararlo — senza doversi giustificare.

Cosa innesca il seguito: la chiusura della campagna, alla sua data di fine o per vostra mano. Le preferenze ancora in bozza diventano allora preferenze vere.

docs.title: 3. L'assegnazione
docs.text:
Chi agisce: il coordinatore.

Due strade, che coesistono.

Il turno automatico serve gli studenti nell'ordine della classifica: il primo ottiene la sua migliore preferenza disponibile, e ciò che resta passa al successivo. Esige da ogni partecipante un profilo, un percorso e una classifica importata — si veda Cosa esige l'abbinamento. Può essere rilanciato tutte le volte che serve.

L'assegnazione manuale non è vincolata da nulla. Collocate chi volete, dove volete, classificato o no.

Cosa innesca il seguito: esiste un'assegnazione.

docs.title: 4. Lo studente accetta — oppure no
docs.text:
Chi agisce: lo studente, salvo se avete scelto l'assegnazione diretta.

Riceve la sua proposta e l'accetta o la rifiuta. Se avete impostato la campagna su assegnazione diretta, questa tappa scompare: la vostra decisione crea l'assegnazione.

Cosa innesca il seguito: l'accettazione.

docs.title: 5. La nomina presso il partner
docs.text:
Chi agisce: il coordinatore, poi l'istituto ospitante.

Nominate lo studente presso la sua destinazione. Il partner riceve l'informazione e risponde — tramite la piattaforma, la rete EWP, e-mail o telefono. Registrate la sua risposta precisando da quale canale è arrivata.

Finché non ha risposto, potete sollecitarlo (una volta ogni ventiquattro ore) o ritirare la nomina, il che rende lo studente disponibile per un'altra destinazione.

Un rifiuto è sempre accompagnato da un motivo, trasmesso all'istituto che ha nominato.

Cosa innesca il seguito: la conferma del partner.

docs.title: 6. La pratica si completa
docs.text:
Chi agisce: lo studente deposita, il coordinatore convalida.

Documenti contrattuali, punteggi linguistici, learning agreement. Ogni elemento atteso è elencato, e lo studente vede cosa gli manca. Sollecitate chi è in ritardo dalla barra di selezione del vostro elenco, senza tenere una lista a parte.

A seconda dell'impostazione della campagna, una pratica incompleta blocca l'assegnazione oppure si limita a essere segnalata.

Cosa innesca il seguito: la pratica è completa e le date si avvicinano.

docs.title: 7. La partenza, poi il soggiorno
docs.text:
Chi agisce: tutti, un po' alla volta.

Lo studente parte. Il suo learning agreement può essere modificato strada facendo — ogni cambio di componente richiede un motivo. Le scadenze del periodo compaiono nell' agenda, e nel calendario a cui ciascuno si è iscritto.

docs.title: 8. Il ritorno
docs.text:
Chi agisce: l'istituto ospitante, poi lo studente.

L'istituto che ha ospitato inserisce i voti nella propria scala ed emette il transcript; lo studente ne è avvisato e lo ritrova nella sua pratica.

Lo studente deposita la sua valutazione sull'istituto ospitante — e può autorizzare la pubblicazione delle sue foto. Chi non ha risposto viene sollecitato come per i documenti.

Cosa chiude il cerchio: la valutazione alimenta la scheda del partner, che gli studenti successivi leggeranno prima di esprimere le loro preferenze.

docs.title: Agenda
docs.text:
L'agenda riunisce tutte le date del vostro istituto in un unico posto: semestri, campagne, scadenze dei vostri partner, tappe di accoglienza, nomine ed eventi.

Finora queste date vivevano in cinque schermate diverse, e nessuno poteva rispondere semplicemente a «cosa scade il mese prossimo?».

docs.title: Cosa ci trovate
docs.text:
A cosa serve. Vedere arrivare le cose. Una scadenza di nomina, la chiusura di una campagna e l'inizio dell'anno di un partner non sono dello stesso ordine, ma cadono nello stesso mese, ed è questo che conta quando si organizza il lavoro.

Per chi. tutto il team mobilità

Come funziona. L'agenda non inventa alcuna data e non ne modifica nessuna: assembla ciò che esiste già altrove. Ogni voce rimanda all'oggetto da cui proviene, ed è lì che la data si modifica — altrimenti due versioni della stessa scadenza finirebbero per contraddirsi.

Passate da una vista elenco a una vista mese, e filtrate per:

  • la famiglia — Semestri, Campagne, Partner, Nomina, Accoglienza, Applicazione, Altro;
  • la direzione — in uscita o in entrata;
  • solo il vostro team, per mettere da parte ciò che non vi riguarda.

I filtri si cumulano, e la barra dei filtri resta sotto gli occhi mentre l'elenco scorre.

Potete anche aggiungere una data a mano, per ciò che non esiste altrove: una riunione di commissione, una scadenza interna.

Il mese in corso, ogni data con il colore della sua famiglia. In alto, i filtri che si cumulano e il pulsante di iscrizione al vostro calendario.

docs.title: Ritrovare le vostre date in Outlook
docs.text:
A cosa serve. Consultare le date di AroundLink dal calendario che già usate, senza aprire lo strumento.

Per chi. tutto il team mobilità, e i vostri studenti

Come funziona. AroundLink pubblica la vostra agenda nel formato standard che tutti i calendari sanno leggere da vent'anni. Copiate l'indirizzo di iscrizione, lo incollate in Outlook, e le vostre date compaiono — aggiornandosi da sole in seguito.

Non è un'integrazione Microsoft: è un formato aperto. Outlook, Google Calendar, Calendario Apple e gli altri sono serviti allo stesso modo, e il vostro servizio informatico non deve autorizzare né configurare nulla.

La sincronizzazione va in un solo senso

Il vostro calendario viene a leggere le date di AroundLink. Non le modifica: una scadenza di nomina non deve poter essere spostata dall'Outlook di uno studente. Per cambiare una data, passate dalla schermata da cui proviene.

Vi iscrivete a ciò che state guardando. L'indirizzo riprende i filtri visualizzati nel momento in cui lo copiate. Potete quindi creare più iscrizioni — «le mie nomine» da una parte, «gli eventi del team» dall'altra — e vederle come due calendari distinti in Outlook, da mostrare o nascondere separatamente.

Cosa contiene il flusso. Soltanto date e il loro titolo. Nessun nome di studente, nessun dato personale transita da questo canale.

Caso d'uso.

La coordinatrice si iscrive all'agenda del suo team filtrata sugli studenti in uscita. Ogni lunedì vede nel suo Outlook le scadenze della settimana senza aprire AroundLink. Quando una data cambia nello strumento, il suo calendario la segue.

L'indirizzo di iscrizione è personale

Dà accesso alla vostra agenda, e solo a quella. Non trasmettetelo: chi lo ricevesse vedrebbe le vostre date. Ciascuno crea il proprio dal proprio account.

docs.title: Wenn etwas nicht funktioniert
docs.text: Die Situationen, die wirklich vorkommen, mit ihrer Ursache und dem, was zu tun ist. Fast alle haben denselben Ursprung: eine vorgelagerte Bedingung ist nicht erfüllt, und der Bildschirm verweigert, statt zu raten.

docs.title: „Ich sehe keine Kampagne"
docs.text:
Drei mögliche Ursachen, nach Häufigkeit geordnet.

Die Kampagne ist nicht geöffnet. Nur der Zustand Geöffnet nimmt Wünsche an. Eine Kampagne im Zustand „Bereit" sehen Sie, Ihre Studierenden nicht.

Die Person gehört nicht zum Teilnehmerkreis. Die Kriterien der Kampagne — Stufe, Studiengang, Campus, Etiketten, Filter — erfassen sie nicht. Öffnen Sie die Kampagne und sehen Sie sich die Teilnehmerliste an: fehlt sie, fügen Sie sie von Hand hinzu.

Die Person hat kein Profil. Ohne Akte existiert sie für keine Kampagne.

docs.title: „Ich kann meine Wünsche nicht abschicken"
docs.text: Sie haben ein Mindestmaß an Wünschen festgelegt, und es ist nicht erreicht. Das Minimum blockiert ebenso wie das Maximum.

docs.title: „Ich finde kein Ziel"
docs.text:
Der Zielkreis der Kampagne ist leer, oder auf den erfassten Abkommen ist kein Platz eingetragen. Prüfen Sie die Platzmatrix, bevor Sie anderswo suchen: ein Ziel ohne Platz wird nicht angezeigt.

Prüfen Sie auch den Zeitraum: ein Platz besteht immer für einen bestimmten Zeitraum.

docs.title: „Ich sehe mein Ranking nicht mehr"
docs.text: Das ist beabsichtigt, wenn Ihre Hochschule das Ranking vor den Studierenden verbirgt. Die Einstellung steht unter Was Ihre Studierenden sehen — Sie und Ihr Team sehen es weiterhin.

docs.title: „Ich habe meinen Zugang nicht erhalten"
docs.text: Ein geöffneter Zugang ist kein empfangener Zugang. Sehen Sie in der Spalte zum Zugangsstatus Ihrer Studierendenliste nach: sie sagt, ob er versandt wurde und wann. Und die Spalte Connected sagt, ob sich die Person bereits angemeldet hat — zwei verschiedene Fragen.

docs.title: „Die Zuteilungsrunde startet nicht"
docs.text:
Das ist die häufigste Blockade, und sie wird immer erklärt: der Bericht nennt die Studierenden, die blockieren, und den Grund.

Meldung Was zu tun ist Die Person hat keinen Studiengang Ordnen Sie ihr einen zu. Nutzt Ihre Hochschule keine, legen Sie einen je Stufe an. Die Person hat kein Ranking Importieren Sie das Ranking vor dem Neustart. Die Runde erzeugt keines. Die Person hat kein Profil Es gibt nichts zu platzieren. Ihre Akte ist unvollständig Vervollständigen Sie sie, oder stellen Sie die Kampagne auf „anzeigen" statt „blockieren".

Die Runde ist keine einmalige Handlung

Beheben Sie, was blockiert, und starten Sie sie so oft neu, wie nötig.

docs.title: „Ich kann diese Kampagne nicht löschen"
docs.text: Nur eine Kampagne im Entwurf lässt sich löschen. Eine geöffnete trägt bereits Wünsche.

docs.title: „Ich kann diese Kampagne nicht wieder öffnen"
docs.text: Nur eine beendete Kampagne lässt sich wieder öffnen. Und wenn Sie das tun, ohne das Enddatum zu verschieben, schließt sie sich am nächsten Morgen erneut.

docs.title: „Meine Kampagne hat sich von selbst geschlossen"
docs.text: Ihr Enddatum ist verstrichen. Das ist seit September 2026 das normale Verhalten: am Tag nach dem letzten Tag schließt die Kampagne, Wünsche im Entwurf werden zu Wünschen, und Sie erhalten die Bilanz. Öffnen Sie sie wieder und verschieben Sie das Datum, falls es zu früh war.

docs.title: „Meine Platzzähler sagen etwas anderes als mein Export"
docs.text: Seit September 2026 erfassen alle Platzzähler ausschließlich ausgehende Mobilitäten — die, die Sie entsenden. Plätze, die Ihre Partner bei sich öffnen, blähen Ihre Summen nicht mehr auf. Überrascht Sie eine Zahl, war sie vermutlich vorher falsch.

docs.title: „Ich kann diesen Partner nicht erinnern"
docs.text: Eine Erinnerung alle vierundzwanzig Stunden. Danach ist die Schaltfläche ausgegraut und sagt Ihnen, ab wann wieder.

docs.title: „Ich kann diese Person nicht auf diesem Abkommen nominieren"
docs.text: Für sie läuft auf diesem Abkommen bereits eine Nominierung. Ziehen Sie sie zuerst zurück, wenn Sie neu nominieren wollen.

docs.title: „Dieser Partner erscheint nicht in meiner Kampagne"
